title: Clocked simulation of a bounded computation
statement: Let $K$ and $W$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ and $s$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $W$ on input $x$. If $c$ is in state $q$, then for every assignment of contents and head positions to the work tapes of $K$, the clock machine started with simulated configuration $c$, an output register recording the contents of $c$’s output tape, and counter tape containing $s$ halts within $4v+2(|s|-r)+|s|+1$ steps and outputs the one-bit word whose bit is true exactly when it is not the case that after $v$ steps from $c$, $W$ has halted and its output is the one-bit word true; here $v$ is the integer represented by $s$ in least-significant-bit-first order and $r$ is the number of true bits in $s$.
hypotheses_covered: contents function for the work tapes of $K$
head-position function for the work tapes of $K$
